arxiv-1803-04459.description: Abstract We propose a new clustering algorithm, Extended Affinity Propagation, based on pairwise similarities. Extended Affinity Propagation is developed by modifying Affinity Propagation such that the desirable features of Affinity Propagation, e.g., exemplars, reasonable computational complexity and no need to specify number of clusters, are preserved while the shortcomings, e.g.

arxiv-2111-12804.title: Evolution of honesty in higher-order social networks
arxiv-2111-12804.creator: Aanjaneya Kumar, Sandeep Chowdhary, Valerio Capraro, Matjaž Perc
arxiv-2111-12804.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aanjaneya Kumar, Sandeep Chowdhary, Valerio Capraro, Matjaž Perc. Sender-receiver games are simple models of information transmission that provide a formalism to study the evolution of honest signaling and deception between a sender and a receiver. In many practical scenarios, lies often affect groups of receivers, which inevitably entangles the payoffs of individuals to the payoffs of other agents in their group, and this makes the formalism of pairwise sender-receiver games inapt for where it might be useful the most.

arxiv-2304-00227.title: Tracker: Model-based Reinforcement Learning for Tracking Control of Human Finger Attached with Thin McKibben Muscles
arxiv-2304-00227.creator: Daichi Saito, Eri Nagatomo, Jefferson Pardomuan, Hideki Koike
arxiv-2304-00227.description: Abstract To adopt the soft hand exoskeleton to support activities of daily livings, it is necessary to control finger joints precisely with the exoskeleton. The problem of controlling joints to follow a given trajectory is called the tracking control problem. In this study, we focus on the tracking control problem of a human finger attached with thin McKibben muscles.

arxiv-2306-02595.title: Explore and Exploit the Diverse Knowledge in Model Zoo for Domain Generalization
arxiv-2306-02595.creator: Yimeng Chen, Tianyang Hu, Fengwei Zhou, Zhenguo Li, Zhiming Ma
arxiv-2306-02595.description: Abstract The proliferation of pretrained models, as a result of advancements in pretraining techniques, has led to the emergence of a vast zoo of publicly available models. Effectively utilizing these resources to obtain models with robust out-of-distribution generalization capabilities for downstream tasks has become a crucial area of research.

arxiv-2310-12205.title: Variations of Interstellar Gas-to-Dust Ratios at High Galactic Latitudes
arxiv-2310-12205.creator: J. Michael Shull, Georgia V. Panopoulou
arxiv-2310-12205.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by J. Michael Shull, Georgia V. Panopoulou. Interstellar dust at high Galactic latitudes can influence astronomical foreground subtraction, produce diffuse scattered light, and soften the ultraviolet spectra of quasars. In a sample of 94 sight lines toward quasars at high latitude and low extinction, we evaluate the interstellar “gas-to-dust ratio” N H / E ⁡ ( B − V ) N_{\rm H}/E(B-V) , using hydrogen column densities (H I and H 2 ) and far-infrared estimates of dust reddening.

arxiv-2408-10513.title: Relativistic and Electron Correlation Effects in Static Dipole Polarizabilities for Main-Group Elements
arxiv-2408-10513.creator: YingXing Cheng
arxiv-2408-10513.description: Abstract In this study, I compute the static dipole polarizability of main-group elements using the finite-field method combined with relativistic coupled-cluster and configuration interaction simulations. The computational results closely align with the values recommended in the 2018 table of static dipole polarizabilities of neutral elements [Mol. Phys. 117, 1200 (2019)].

arxiv-2502-13924.creator: Robert Jarolim ∗, Momchil E. Molnar ∗, Benoit Tremblay, Rebecca Centeno, Matthias Rempel
arxiv-2502-13924.description: Abstract Spectropolarimetric inversions of solar observations are fundamental for the estimation of the magnetic field in the solar atmosphere. However, instrumental noise, computational requirements, and varying levels of physical realism make it challenging to derive reliable solar magnetic field estimates.

arxiv-2505-18694.title: AI-Driven Climate Policy Scenario Generation for Sub-Saharan Africa
arxiv-2505-18694.creator: Rafiu Adekoya Badekale, Adewale Akinfaderin
arxiv-2505-18694.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rafiu Adekoya Badekale, Adewale Akinfaderin. Climate policy scenario generation and evaluation have traditionally relied on integrated assessment models (IAMs) and expert-driven qualitative analysis. These methods enable stakeholders, such as policymakers and researchers, to anticipate impacts, plan governance strategies, and develop mitigation measures. However, traditional methods are often time-intensive, reliant on simple extrapolations of past trends, and limited in capturing the complex and interconnected nature of energy and climate issues.

arxiv-2507-06848.title: Know Your Attention Maps: Class-specific Token Masking for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2507-06848.creator: Joëlle Hanna, Damian Borth
arxiv-2507-06848.description: Abstract Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) is a challenging problem that has been extensively studied in recent years. Traditional approaches often rely on external modules like Class Activation Maps [ 36 ] to highlight regions of interest and generate pseudo segmentation masks.

arxiv-2508-17197.title: Optimal Circuit Size for Fixed-Hamming-Weight Quantum States Preparation
arxiv-2508-17197.creator: Jingquan Luo, Lvzhou Li
arxiv-2508-17197.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jingquan Luo, Lvzhou Li. We study the problem of efficiently preparing fixed-Hamming-weight (HW- k k ) quantum states, which are superpositions of n n -qubit computational basis states with exactly k k ones. We present a quantum circuit construction that prepares any n n -qubit HW- k k state with a circuit size of O ⁡ ( ( n k ) ) O(\binom{n}{k}) using at most max ⁡ { 0 , n − 3 } \max\{0,n-3\} ancillary qubits.

arxiv-2510-18065.title: Can the CMB be Odd? Effect of a Parity-Violating Matter 4-Point Function on the Low- ℓ \ell CMB Trispectrum
arxiv-2510-18065.creator: Zachary Slepian, Matthew Reinhard, Michael Bartlett
arxiv-2510-18065.description: Abstract Here we explore from a theoretical perspective the sensitivity of the primary CMB anisotropy trispectrum to parity violation (PV) in large-scale structure (LSS). We focus on the Sachs-Wolfe term, which dominates at ℓ < 40 \ell<40 , after which the Doppler term takes over.

pmc-11609530.title: Mechanistic insight into multiple antibody binding to ADAMTS13 in immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
pmc-11609530.creator: Konstantine Halkidis, Chan Meng, Vikram G. Pillai, Madison Shay, Szumam Liu, X. Long Zheng
pmc-11609530.description: BackgroundAntibody-mediated inhibition of von Willebrand factor (VWF) cleavage by ADAMTS-13 results in immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP). However, the effects of multiple antibody binding to ADAMTS-13 are not fully understood.ObjectivesTo determine how multiple antibodies affect ADAMTS13 activity under various conditions.

pmc-12458803.title: Prevalence of and factors influencing elevated blood pressure among Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12458803.creator: Lijuan Zheng, Weiwei Xiang, Rui Zheng, Xinwen Min, Li Dai, Jun Chen, Juanjuan Lu, Yujue Wang, Xiang Liu, Wenwen Wu, Hao Xu
pmc-12458803.description: AbstractObjectiveThis study aims to examine the prevalence of elevated blood pressure (BP) among adolescents aged 13–17 years in Shiyan city, Hubei province, China. Additionally, it analyses the distribution characteristics and potential factors influencing elevated BP, providing a scientific foundation for the prevention and management of hypertension in adolescents.DesignCross-sectional study.SettingA total of 11 schools in central China.

pmc-12499888.title: eCarbonyls: an electrochemical thioether mediated oxidation of alcohols to aldehydes and ketones
pmc-12499888.creator: Conall Molloy, Simon Kaltenberger, Lee Edwards, Katherine M. P. Wheelhouse, Kevin Lam
pmc-12499888.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We report eCarbonyls, a scalable, metal-free electrochemical oxidation of alcohols that mimics key features of the classical Swern reaction while avoiding its reliance on cryogenic conditions and hazardous reagents. Operating at room temperature in an undivided cell, this process employs a stable thioether mediator to generate reactive radical cation intermediates that enable selective oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols to aldehydes and ketones.

pmc-12568678.title: Genetic association and functional implications of AhR gene polymorphism on preeclampsia
pmc-12568678.creator: Hong Jiang, Haiyun Meng, Yantuanjin Ma, Yuan Qian, Xuerong Chen, Lan Luo, Yuling Yang
pmc-12568678.description: BackgroundPreeclampsia is one of the main causes of increased maternal and infant mortality and morbidity during pregnancy. The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor ubiquitously found in mammals that can directly or indirectly regulate various physiological processes when activated.MethodsIn this case-control study, 74 patients with preeclampsia and 120 healthy pregnant controls were recruited.

pmc-13150188.title: Development of AI-based tools for assessing temporomandibular joint disorders using MRI images
pmc-13150188.creator: Aditya Narayan Shukla, Vishwannath Hiremath, Vineet Vaibhav, Shiwangi Kumari, Bassam Alkhalifah, Pranay Yajurvedi
pmc-13150188.description: Temporomandibular joint disorders (TMDs) are diagnostically challenging due to the complexity of MRI interpretation and high inter- observer variability among clinicians. Therefore, it is of interest to develop and evaluate artificial intelligence-based tools for automated assessment of TMDs using magnetic resonance imaging.

pmc-13335837.title: Machine learning-driven dual-objective optimization of biomass-derived carbon quantum dots toward high conductivity and yield
pmc-13335837.creator: Heng Jiang, Haoyu Zhang, Ninghui Xu, Yanji Hao, Boyuan Zhang, Jianping Su, Yeqing Li
pmc-13335837.description: Biomass-derived carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have been reported to effectively improve the efficiency of anaerobic digestion processes. However, simultaneously achieving high CQD yield and high conductivity remains challenging due to the complexity of the process. To address this, a machine learning approach was employed to optimize the preparation of straw-based CQDs.

pmc-13351923.title: Müllerian Agenesis Presenting as Primary Amenorrhea in a 16‐Year‐Old Girl From a Low‐Resource Setting in Bangladesh: Psychological Impact and Multidisciplinary Management
pmc-13351923.creator: Iftekhar Ahmed Sakib, Musarrat Sultana Shumi, Rozina Sultana, Ayesa Perveen, Nishad Tasnim, Shirazum Munira
pmc-13351923.description: Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome) causes primary amenorrhea in phenotypically normal females. We report a 16‐year‐old girl with normal secondary sexual characteristics, a short blind vagina, absent uterus on ultrasonography, and a 46,XX karyotype. Successful vaginoplasty and counseling in a low‐resource setting highlight the importance of systematic evaluation and multidisciplinary management.

pmc-13352885.title: Concurrent lumbar degenerative disease is independently associated with chronic post-surgical pain after total knee arthroplasty for knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective study
pmc-13352885.creator: Xichen Zhang, Xinfei Zhu, Dunliang Rao, Lei Sha, Liang Hao, Shouhai Jiang, Ziyang Zhang, Chuankai Zhang
pmc-13352885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveChronic post-surgical pain (CPSP) after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains a significant clinical challenge. This study aimed to investigate the association between concurrent lumbar degenerative disease (LDD) and CPSP after TKA for knee osteoarthritis (KOA).MethodsA total of 348 KOA patients undergoing first unilateral TKA (June 2023-June 2025) were enrolled and stratified into LDD (n = 167) and non-LDD (n = 181) groups. CPSP incidence, pain severity, and postoperative knee function were compared.

pmc-13680382.title: Contribution of cohesins STAG1 and STAG2 to preimplantation development in mice
pmc-13680382.creator: Maria Solé-Ferran, Maria José Andreu, Daniel Giménez-Llorente, Jaime Muñoz, Sagrario Ortega, Ana Losada
pmc-13680382.description: Cohesin complexes carrying either STAG1 or STAG2 display functional specificities in both cohesion and genome organization. While any variant is sufficient for cell viability, both are essential for murine embryonic development, and mutations in STAG1 and STAG2 are associated to human syndromes. The requirements and regulation of the cohesin variants in the first stages of development remain unknown.
